question: Lipids are transferred from intestine to liver by
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Dietary fats" -> "absorbed in intestine" -> "packaged into chylomicrons" -> "transported via lymphatic system" -> "enter bloodstream" -> "delivered to liver" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Intestinal absorption" -> "formation of chylomicrons" -> "transport through lymphatics" -> "enter systemic circulation" -> "reach liver" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Chylomicrons" -> "carry triglycerides" -> "enter bloodstream" -> "deliver lipids to liver" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Intestinal lipids" -> "chylomicron formation" -> "lymphatic transport" -> "systemic circulation" -> "liver uptake" -> 92%
analysis: Lipids absorbed from the intestine are packaged into chylomicrons, which are lipoprotein particles. These chylomicrons transport dietary lipids through the lymphatic system and into the bloodstream, eventually reaching the liver. VLDL, HDL, and LDL are involved in lipid transport within the bloodstream but are not responsible for the initial transfer of lipids from the intestine to the liver.
